toolDefinitions.description:
An agent is a model session that works in the background. Each agent in the list below has a name and a description of the work that it does. Give an agent a whole unit of work: work that needs many reads, a long output, or a loop of fixes and tests. Do a task of one step yourself. Give the work to the agent whose description matches it. When the list does not show all the agents or their descriptions, or when no agent in the list matches the work, call the tool "agents" with the arguments {"op": "list agents"}. When no agent matches the work after that, do the work yourself. Each agent starts with an empty context and sees only the prompt that you give it, so put the full task and all that the agent needs in the prompt. When the agent changes files, tell it in the prompt to commit after each step that works, so that each commit is a point to undo to. To give a task to an agent, call the tool "agents" with the arguments {"op": "start agent", "name": "<name>", "prompt": "<the full task>"}. The value of "op" is an operation of the tool "agents", not the name of a tool. When the agent finishes in a few seconds, the call gives its final message. Else the call gives a pending answer, and the agent works in the background. Its result will arrive in this conversation as a message when it is ready. You do not need to wait for it or check on it, and no tool can make it come sooner. Go on with any work that does not need it. If none is left, post your status as plain text: what you wait on and its completion token.

- coder: Use to make a code changes.
- committer: Use to commit finished code.
- general-purpose: Use for non coding multi-step tasks. Start several to work in parallel.
- leaf: The leaf agent of the nested recording.
- tester: Use to run tests.

The session that started you has the id 01M6KZ8Z4GXEZCXF3F53NAEBVM. Send a message to it with {"op": "send caller", "message": "..."}.
